newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian council quits over "racist" mayor.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian council quits over "racist" mayor.

text.p: An Australian town council has resigned en masse after its mayor wrote a letter describing children of inter-racial marriages as "mongrels", further fanning a national debate on racism.
Nine out of the 10 members of the council in Port Lincoln, 700 kms (435 miles) east of Adelaide, quit on Monday night after the mayor refused to resign, a councillor said on Wednesday.
"We decided enough is enough and when he would not resign or retract, the only thing we thought we could do as honourable people was to resign," councillor Rod Cocks told Reuters.
"I would go as far as to say he is an extremist and a fascist in the true definition of the word," Cocks said

Mayor Peter Davis, a local headmaster, used a council letterhead to endorse maverick politician Pauline Hanson in her controversial criticism of Asian migration and government assistance for Aborigines.
Davis defended using the word "mongrel" in the letter to Hanson, saying it was like using the word bastard to describe illegitimate children.
"If you are a child of a mixed race...Asian-Caucasian or aboriginal-white, you are a mongrel and that's what happens when you cross dogs or whatever," Davis told reporters on Wednesday.
"I'm not a racist, I don't believe I'm superior to a person of another culture, but I do recognise that cultures are different," Davis said.

Davis, principal of the Port Lincoln high school, said he was not opposed to immigration, but he thought Australians should be allowed to debate openly whether they wanted to cut the level of immigration to fight unemployment.
Port Lincoln is a fishing and farming town of 13,000 people from about 50 ethnic backgrounds in South Australia state.
The Federation of Ethnic Communities Council of Australia said it would ask the state government to sack Davis from his post as mayor.
